findings.text: the done-when table states "minute rows: 12 samples and 60 s each; hour rows: 720 samples and 3,600 s each", but a 20 s cadence gives 3 and 180 samples - as tests/test_telemetry_store.py:228 asserts (60 // _CADENCE_S) and as measured here (review_probe3.log: minute obs {'samples': 3, 'seconds': 60.0}, hour obs {'samples': 180, 'seconds': 3600.0}, both tiers summing to the 12,960 raw rows) - the seconds and the sum property are right and only the two sample counts are wrong; 12 and 720 are what a 5 s raw resolution would give, so the figures come from the plan's tier table rather than from the record this node built, and they survived into the commit (792a48a0) whose stated subject is correcting this very record.

main() is the entry point the done-when item "the subcommand rebuilds a tier from its source" rests on, and no test calls it - tests/test_telemetry_store.py imports compact_file, compact_rows, read_rows and run_compaction but never main - so a regression in its argument parsing or in the delegate it makes would leave the suite green while the documented rebuild path broke; this review node exercises it by hand (review_probe.log: main() returns 0 and writes a row) which is the assertion the suite is missing.VERDICT goal: read from the dispatch prompt and plan §4 ("Compact a raw record through minute and hour tiers without distorting what it averages") - the landed module compacts the raw JSONL record into minute and hour tiers with counters endpointed and gauges time-weighted, and both behaviours were re-derived here rather than accepted.
